The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Culver City, California I'm Dua Lea Saikow Tao.
President Trump's son-in-law and peace envoy Jared Kushner says
Russian President Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" in the war against Ukraine
by not using nuclear weapons.
Kushner was speaking on a podcast hosted by the CEO of the company that owns Politico,
as Willem Marx reports.
On the MD Meets podcast with Axel Springer Chief Matthias Dopfner,
Kushner called Putin a "grandmaster of politics" and credited him with holding himself back.
"So far Putin has showed restraint. He's agreed not to use nuclear weapons,
which obviously is a big thing, and he's reassured us that that's not his intention."
Kushner said he believes Putin wants peace between Russia and Ukraine.
He also said peace talks should focus most of all on ending the war,
not deciding which side is right or wrong.
But this little sign the war itself is winding down.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky said in his nightly address to the nation Thursday
that Russia was preparing a new mass strike in the coming days.
He also urged Ukrainians to pay attention to missile alerts.
For NPR News, I'm Willem Marx.
For the first time in history, the annual Macy's Day Thanksgiving Parade
has been postponed due to severe weather.
The executive producer of the parade, Will Koss, says it is now scheduled for Saturday.
"Since 1924, the parade has continued to march down the streets of New York City,
where a rain or shine event. We don't even postpone for three years during World War II.
And that was an opportunity for us to donate some of our materials to the war effort.
So this was an unprecedented situation."
He said his team acted quickly in hopes for a successful 100th parade on Saturday.
New York mayor Zoran Mamdani said he knows New Yorkers and millions around the world
were looking forward to the parade today, but he added, "Safety has to come first."
Judges in Israel are calling to drop some of the corruption charges
against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The trial against him has been going on for six years.
Netanyahu denies wrongdoing, and Piers Daniel-Estron reports from Tel Aviv.
In a surprise move, the judges overseeing Netanyahu's corruption trial
called on Israel's attorney general to consider dropping the most serious case of bribery,
where Netanyahu was accused of trading business favors with a media mogul
in exchange for positive news coverage.
In the second case involving Netanyahu's dealings with a newspaper owner,
the judges said they doubted a crime was committed.
And the judges recommended the sides settle the final case,
where Netanyahu was accused of getting gifts from a Hollywood producer
and helping him with an Israeli tax break.
This is promising news for Netanyahu,
but he may be unseated as Prime Minister as early as next week.
His rival, Gadi Eisenkot, is trying to form a new government.
Daniel-Estron, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
And you are listening to NPR from Culver City, California.
An enthusiastic coonhound named Rocker is top dog at this year's National Dog Show.
NPR's Chloe Veltman reports the victorious canine with a glossy black and tan coat
and big floppy ears beat out six other dogs to take the title.
Rocker's handler Mandy Clevenger told NBC the coonhound had a great time
at the 2026 National Dog Show.
Rocker loves the crowd.
He loves the people, loves other dogs and kids.
So this is a great venue for him.
Best in show, Judge Lorraine Bisso praised Rocker's handsome looks and physical prowess.
She also commended Clevenger for fading into the background
and allowing the dog to shine,
a remarkable feat considering the fact the handler was wearing a bright yellow suit.
The annual event was held in person at the Greater Philadelphia Expo Center earlier this month.
NBC has telecast it each year on Thanksgiving Day since 2002.
Owing to the rescheduled Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade,
NBC plans to re-air the show on Saturday starting at noon.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
A driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker to overturn
and cause a deadly inferno on a major highway in Egypt is now in custody.
Egyptian authorities said the crash took place during rush hour
on the multi-lane Ring Road in Cairo, killing at least 31 people yesterday.
An eyewitness told the Associated Press it was God's hellfire on Ring Road,
saying people are still in shock.
AP video shows soot and ash lining the roadway today as traffic returned.
Investigators say at least 27 vehicles were burned.
You're listening to NPR News.
I'm Dua Lisa Kautau.

Zelensky warns Russia is preparing a new mass missile strike on Ukraine in coming days

Israeli judges urge attorney general to consider dropping Netanyahu's most serious bribery charge
Israeli judges doubt a crime in second Netanyahu case and recommend settling the final case
Rocker, a coonhound, wins best in show at the National Dog Show in Philadelphia
Egypt arrests driver suspected of causing fuel tanker crash and deadly fire on Cairo Ring Road
